entries.officialText:
For each real \(x\) such that \(-1 < x < 1\), let \(A(x) = (1 - x)^{-1/2} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -x \\ -x & 1 \end{pmatrix}\), then \(A(x)A(y) = \sqrt{1 + xy} \, A(t)\), where \(t =\)
(A) \(\frac{x - y}{1 - xy}\)
(B) \(\frac{x + y}{1 + xy}\)
(C) \(\frac{x - y}{1 + xy}\)
(D) \(\frac{x + y}{1 - xy}\)
entries.reasoning: Multiplying the two matrices gives (1+xy) times the same matrix with t = (x+y)/(1+xy), and the prefactor is exactly the one that turns (1-x)(1-y) into (1+xy).
entries.verification: Solved by hand from the corpus text; no numeric formulation, so the reasoning above is the whole audit trail.
entries.note: Provisional: solved from the corpus text layer, not the printed page. No page image was available, so this answer may not be scored.

(A) \(\sum \hat{i} (\hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 0\)
(B) \(\sum \hat{i} (\hat{j} \times \hat{k}) = 0\)
(C) \(\sum \hat{i} \times (\hat{j} \times \hat{k}) = \vec{0}\)
(D) \(\sum \hat{i} \times (\hat{j} + \hat{k}) = \vec{0}\)
entries.reasoning: The sum of i.(j x k) over the cyclic permutations is 1+1+1 = 3, not zero, while the other three sums do vanish.
